svg.desc: Banner for a paper on the L_p-spherical copula conjecture. Title: close, but never exact. Left text: with both marginals fixed, which dependence makes two random points lie farthest apart? At power 1 the answer is the disc copula, the shadow of a uniform sphere. For other powers, the conjectured answer was the L_p-spherical law with p = 3 minus beta. Proved: it fails at every beta other than 1, and no member of the family is ever optimal off beta = 1. Numerically the loss is tiny, parts per million; the family stays an excellent approximation. Centre: the outlines of the supports for p = 1.5, 2 (the disc) and 2.5 inside the square, with a dot on the vertical axis marking the kink in the density that the proof detects. Right: a chart of how far the conjectured law falls short of an explicit better copula, in parts per million of the optimum on a log scale, at six powers between 0.25 and 1.75: about 25.5, 12.8, 2.0, 0.2, 1.8 and 12.4, with a dashed line at power 1 where the disc copula is exact. Footer: proofs for every beta other than 1; the sizes are floating-point estimates on discretised copulas, not certified bounds; unrefereed candidate.
